Challah

Made in the Magimix 5200XL — the machine does the mixing and the 10-minute knead in about 1 minute.

Makes1 plaited loaf · 18–20 slices Hands-on≈ 20 min Rising1 hr + 40 min Bake25–30 min · 200C / 180C fan / gas 6

Ingredients

Magimix setup: main 3.6L bowl + dough blade (the short blunt metal blade). 500g flour is comfortably within the 5200XL's dough capacity.
Golden rule: knead in short bursts and stop once smooth — the blade works fast, and over-running heats the dough.
Friday shortcut: steps 1–4 take about 15 minutes. Do them in the morning, let the first rise happen slowly in the fridge all day, then plait, prove and bake before dinner.

Method

  1. Wake the yeastStir the yeast and a pinch of the sugar into 2 tbsp lukewarm water. Leave about 10 minutes until foamy.
  2. Dry mixFit the dough blade. Tip the flour, remaining sugar and salt into the bowl and pulse 2–3 times to combine.
  3. Bring it togetherAdd half the beaten egg, the foamy yeast mixture and the oil. Run the motor and pour 200ml lukewarm water steadily through the feed tube. Within 20–30 seconds the dough should gather into a ball that rides around on the blade. Still floury? Water 1 tbsp at a time with short pulses. Sticky and smearing? Flour 1 tbsp at a time. Moist but not soggy.
  4. Machine kneadOnce the ball forms, keep the motor running a further 45–60 seconds — this replaces the 10-minute hand knead. Done when smooth and it springs back from a gentle poke. Slightly warm is normal.
  5. First riseTurn out, give it 2–3 turns by hand on a lightly floured surface and shape into a tight ball. Roll around a lightly oiled bowl to coat, cover with a tea towel, and leave somewhere warm about 1 hour, until doubled.
  6. PlaitLine a baking sheet with parchment. Divide into 3 equal pieces (weigh them) and roll each into a 25cm rope, slightly tapered at the ends. Don't over-flour — slightly tacky ropes grip each other, so the plait won't split. Pinch together at the top, plait to the bottom, tuck both ends under. Lift onto the sheet.
  7. Second riseCover loosely and leave until puffy and billowy, about 40 minutes. Meanwhile heat the oven to 200C / 180C fan / gas 6.
  8. Glaze & bakeBrush the reserved beaten egg all over, into every crevice; scatter the seeds if using. Bake on the middle shelf 25–30 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath. Check at 15 minutes — tent with foil if darkening fast. Cool on a wire rack.

House rules — the challah & babka doughs

  • Dough blade, main 3.6L bowl. Comfortable up to ~1kg of dough (500g flour is fine). Yeast and salt on opposite sides; pulse the dry mix 2–3×.
  • Liquids through the feed tube, motor running — a ball rides the blade in 20–30s. Floury → water 1 tbsp at a time; smearing → flour 1 tbsp at a time.
  • 45–60 seconds replaces the 10-minute knead. Short bursts, always — the blade heats dough fast. Stop at smooth and springy.
  • Butter goes in via the feed tube, a few soft cubes at a time — then chill butter-rich doughs 30 min before rolling.
  • Our oven runs cool. Times are for the no-fan (conventional) setting — on fan, drop 20C. Trust the probe, not the clock: bread is done at 90–93C in the centre. Tent with foil if the top darkens early.
  • Overnight fridge proof is the house default — knead in the evening, shape and bake in the morning.
  • Yeast comes in 7g sachets. Recipes calling for 5g: the full sachet is fine — prove by size, not the clock.

Adapted for the Magimix 5200XL from BBC Good Food's challah (bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/challah) · photo: our own bake, Aug 2026 · The Hancox

Cloud Challahs

Keren Agam's Friday challahs — very soft, only lightly sweet, cold-water dough. Translated from mako and rebuilt at half her quantities, which is one comfortable Magimix batch.

Makes2 plaited loaves · ≈450g each Hands-on≈ 25 min Rising1½–2 h + 30 min + 30–35 min Bake25–35 min · 190C no fan / 170C fan

Ingredients

Magimix: ≈915g of dough, comfortably inside the 5200XL's 1.2kg bread-dough rating. Main 3.6L bowl, dough blade, one batch — no splitting.
The cold water is deliberate — and it suits us. The blade heats dough fast; fridge-cold water is what keeps this one workable. Don't warm it.
Only 13% sugar, so it behaves like the plain one. Standard machine method; no late-sugar trick needed.
Yeast: one 7g sachet, same as our other two challahs. Keren uses a more generous 2% (10g here), so expect the proves to run at the longer end of the times given — go by size, not the clock.
Overnight (house default): after the knead, cover and refrigerate. Next day divide and shape cold, then pick up at step 4 — allow a little longer on both proves.
Source: Keren Agam, mako — "Classic Friday Cloud Challahs", halved. Her glazing egg and sesame appear in her method but not her ingredient list; both are in ours. Her serving note: the first loaf goes at Friday lunch, in sandwiches with schnitzel and matbucha.

Method

  1. Dry mixDough blade in the main bowl. Flour, yeast, sugar and salt — yeast and salt on opposite sides — and pulse 2–3 times.
  2. Bring it togetherAdd the egg and oil. With the motor running, pour about 180ml of the 240ml cold water through the feed tube, keeping the rest back. A ball should gather and ride the blade in 20–30 seconds. Still floury? Add the reserved water a tablespoon at a time. The dough should be uniform and a little sticky — that is Keren's own description, and it is right.
  3. Machine knead45–60 seconds in short bursts once the ball forms — this replaces her 10–12 minutes in a stand mixer. Turn into a lightly oiled bowl.
  4. First riseCover and leave at room temperature 1½–2 hours, until doubled.
  5. Divide and restDivide into 6 balls of ≈150g. Set them on an oiled, parchment-lined tray, oil the tops, cover loosely with a bag or cling film. Prove 30 minutes.
  6. Roll the strandsRoll each ball out to a rectangle, then roll it up into a strand. Keep them short and plump, not long and thin — that is what gives these loaves their height.
  7. PlaitTwo loaves, three strands each. Lift onto a large parchment-lined tray.
  8. Final prove30–35 minutes, until visibly puffy. Poke test: a floured finger 1cm in should spring back slowly, leaving a faint dent. Meanwhile heat the oven to 190C, no fan.
  9. Glaze & bakeBrush with the second egg, beaten, and scatter sesame. Bake 25–35 minutes until deep golden — but trust the probe, not the clock: 90–93C in the centre. These are smaller loaves than our other challah, so start checking at 25 minutes; our oven runs cool, so don't be surprised by the longer end. Cool on a wire rack.

Chocolate Babka

Paul Hollywood's babka, rebuilt for the Magimix 5200XL — nut-free — the machine makes the dough and works in the butter.

Makes1 loaf · 900g tin Hands-on≈ 30 min Chill30 min Prove≈ 2 hr Bake40–45 min · no fan

Ingredients

Dough
Filling
Syrup
Magimix setup: dough blade in the main bowl (≈540g of dough — easily within capacity).
Why the chill: the blade works the dough warm and this one is rich with butter — 30 min in the fridge firms it so the rolling and twisting stay neat.
Overnight option: prove the shaped loaf in its tin in the fridge overnight, then bake from cold in the morning — add 5–10 min and trust the skewer, not the clock.

Method

  1. Make the fillingGently melt the butter, sugar and chocolate in a small pan. Off the heat, stir in the cocoa. Leave to cool until thick and spreadable.
  2. Dry mixFit the dough blade. Add the flour, sugar, yeast and salt (yeast and salt on opposite sides) and pulse 2–3 times.
  3. DoughAdd the beaten eggs and milk and run about 30 seconds, until a soft dough gathers on the blade.
  4. Butter inWith the motor running, drop the butter cubes through the feed tube a few at a time. Run a further 45–60 seconds until smooth, silky and shiny — soft and slightly sticky is exactly right. This replaces the whole stand-mixer knead.
  5. ChillScrape into a bowl, cover, and refrigerate 30 minutes to firm up for rolling.
  6. Fill, roll & twistGrease and line a 900g loaf tin. Roll the dough to a 40 × 30cm rectangle. Spread the filling leaving a 1cm border and roll up tightly from a long edge. Trim the ends, then slice the log in half lengthwise. Cut (stripy) sides up, twist the two halves over each other, pinch the ends, lift into the tin cut-sides up.
  7. ProveCover loosely and leave at room temperature about 2 hours, until doubled and risen to the top of the tin.
  8. BakeHeat the oven to 190C, no fan. Bake 15 minutes, then turn down to 170C for another 25–30 minutes, until a skewer into the centre comes out with no wet dough (chocolate is fine). Our oven runs cool — expect the top end, and give it 10 extra minutes if the skewer says so. Tent with foil if the top darkens early.
  9. SyrupWhile it bakes, boil the sugar and water, then simmer 5 minutes. Brush all of the syrup over the hot babka in its tin — it looks like too much; it isn't. Cool completely before slicing.

House rules — the challah & babka doughs

  • Dough blade, main 3.6L bowl. Comfortable up to ~1kg of dough (500g flour is fine). Yeast and salt on opposite sides; pulse the dry mix 2–3×.
  • Liquids through the feed tube, motor running — a ball rides the blade in 20–30s. Floury → water 1 tbsp at a time; smearing → flour 1 tbsp at a time.
  • 45–60 seconds replaces the 10-minute knead. Short bursts, always — the blade heats dough fast. Stop at smooth and springy.
  • Butter goes in via the feed tube, a few soft cubes at a time — then chill butter-rich doughs 30 min before rolling.
  • Our oven runs cool. Times are for the no-fan (conventional) setting — on fan, drop 20C. Trust the probe, not the clock: bread is done at 90–93C in the centre. Tent with foil if the top darkens early.
  • Overnight fridge proof is the house default — knead in the evening, shape and bake in the morning.
  • Yeast comes in 7g sachets. Recipes calling for 5g: the full sachet is fine — prove by size, not the clock.

Adapted for the Magimix 5200XL from Paul Hollywood's Chocolate Babka (thegreatbritishbakeoff.co.uk) · The Hancox

Next-Level Chocolate Babka

BBC Good Food's babka, rebuilt for the Magimix 5200XL — dough in the main bowl, filling in the mini bowl, and an overnight rise that fits the routine. Contains almonds.

Serves8 · 900g tin Hands-on≈ 30 min Chillovernight Prove2–3 hr Bake≈45 min · 180C no fan · 90C inside

Ingredients

Dough
Filling
Syrup
Magimix setup: dough blade in the main bowl for the dough; mini bowl + mini blade for the filling paste. No stand mixer needed.
The chill is the recipe: this dough is designed to rest in the fridge overnight — cold, firm dough is what gives the sharp chocolate layers.
Same-day fallback: no overnight? Rise 2 hrs at room temp, then chill at least 1 hr — never roll it warm.

Method

  1. Dry mixFit the dough blade. Add the flour, cinnamon (if using), sugar, yeast and salt (yeast and salt on opposite sides) and pulse 2–3 times.
  2. DoughAdd the milk and eggs and run 30–45 seconds until a smooth, soft dough forms on the blade. Rest it in the bowl, lid on, for 10 minutes — this replaces the long mixer knead.
  3. Butter inWith the motor running, drop the butter cubes through the feed tube a few at a time, then run 45–60 seconds until silky and shiny. Soft and sticky is correct.
  4. Overnight chillScrape into a buttered bowl, cover, and refrigerate overnight, until nearly doubled.
  5. Filling (mini bowl)Melt the chocolate (bain-marie, or 10-second microwave bursts) and let it cool. In the mini bowl, blitz the butter, sugar and ground almonds; add the cocoa, melted chocolate and a pinch of sea salt and pulse to a spreadable paste.
  6. Fill & rollRoll the cold dough on a floured surface to a 30 × 40cm rectangle, long edge towards you. Spread the filling to a thin border, scatter the flaked almonds, and roll away from you into a tight log. If there's fridge space, chill the log 1 hour, seam-side down — it sharpens the layers.
  7. TwistButter a 900g loaf tin, line with a parchment strip overhanging both ends. Cut the log in half lengthwise with a serrated knife, lay the pieces parallel, and plait to about 8 twists. Lift into the tin, tuck the ends under, fatten the plait to fit.
  8. ProveCover with a tea towel and leave at room temperature 2–3 hours, until risen by about half.
  9. BakeHeat the oven to 180C, no fan. Bake about 45 minutes until dark golden — done at 90C on a probe in the middle. Our oven runs cool: trust the probe, not the clock, and tent with foil if the top darkens early.
  10. SyrupBoil the sugar with 4 tbsp water until dissolved. Brush over the hot babka in stages, letting each coat soak in, until it's all gone. Cool fully before slicing. Best on the day; keeps 2 days airtight.

House rules — the challah & babka doughs

  • Dough blade, main 3.6L bowl. Comfortable up to ~1kg of dough (500g flour is fine). Yeast and salt on opposite sides; pulse the dry mix 2–3×.
  • Liquids through the feed tube, motor running — a ball rides the blade in 20–30s. Floury → water 1 tbsp at a time; smearing → flour 1 tbsp at a time.
  • 45–60 seconds replaces the 10-minute knead. Short bursts, always — the blade heats dough fast. Stop at smooth and springy.
  • Butter goes in via the feed tube, a few soft cubes at a time — then chill butter-rich doughs 30 min before rolling.
  • Our oven runs cool. Times are for the no-fan (conventional) setting — on fan, drop 20C. Trust the probe, not the clock: bread is done at 90–93C in the centre. Tent with foil if the top darkens early.
  • Overnight fridge proof is the house default — knead in the evening, shape and bake in the morning.
  • Yeast comes in 7g sachets. Recipes calling for 5g: the full sachet is fine — prove by size, not the clock.

Adapted for the Magimix 5200XL from BBC Good Food's Next-level chocolate babka (bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/next-level-chocolate-babka) · The Hancox

Biscuit Cake

Esti Rotem's nostalgic no-bake classic from mako Food — let the kids make it, almost no help needed. Biscuits, a creamy vanilla filling, and chocolate on top.

Tin30 × 18cm rectangular Hands-on≈ 20 min Chill3 hr minimum Ovennone — no-bake

Ingredients

Base
Filling
Topping
UK shopping (house note — this is an Israeli recipe): biscuits = petit beurre or Rich Tea. Cream: the sweet cream this recipe uses in Israel is 32% fat — UK whipping cream (~35%) is the match; double cream (48%) whips too heavy, single (18%) won't whip. White cheese (gvina levana, ~5%): use Fage Total 5% Greek yogurt (weigh out 500g) or quark. Pudding = the powdered instant vanilla mix (Osem/Jell-O) — kosher shops, American aisles or Amazon, not a supermarket staple.
Why this whipping order (mako editors): the original whips everything together — most get a great result, some find it too loose. Whipping the cream, pudding, milk and sugar first, then adding the cheese, keeps it stable.
Keeps: in the fridge. Freezing not recommended.

Method

  1. Whip the creamWhip the whipping cream with the pudding mix, milk and sugar to a stable whipped cream. Add the cheese and lemon zest and whip only until incorporated.
  2. Dip & layerIn a deep plate, mix the ½ cup milk with the vanilla and the shot of coffee. Dip each biscuit — a quick, short dunk — and lay in a 30 × 18cm rectangular tin to form a layer of biscuits.
  3. FillGently spread half the cream over the biscuits. Cover with a second layer of dipped biscuits. Spread the rest of the cream and cover with a third biscuit layer.
  4. Chocolate top & chillGrate 70% dark chocolate generously over the top — our way. (The original melts 100g chocolate with 120ml cream in 30-second microwave bursts until glossy, and pours it over.) Refrigerate at least 3 hours.

Translated for The Hancox from Esti Rotem's biscuit cake on mako Food (mako.co.il, first published 2012) · rated 4.6 by 11,500+ home cooks

Banana Oatmeal Pancakes

Monique Volz's blender pancakes from Ambitious Kitchen — the whole batter is blitzed smooth, no flour, naturally sweetened by ripe bananas. Contains almond milk.

Makes9 pancakes · serves 3 Prep10 min Cook10 min Ovennone — pan or griddle

Ingredients

No blender? (house note): the Magimix main bowl with the standard metal blade should handle this batter — blitz until the oats disappear and it pours smoothly.
Freezer-friendly: freeze the cooked pancakes flat on a tray for 30 minutes so they don't stick together, then bag them up — keeps up to 3 months.

Method

  1. BlendAdd all the ingredients to a blender and blend on high until completely smooth, about 30 seconds to 1 minute. Let the batter sit in the blender while the pan heats up.
  2. First sideLightly coat a griddle or pan with coconut oil, vegan butter or olive oil over medium heat. Once hot, add ⅓ cup of batter per pancake and cook 2–4 minutes, until they slightly puff up and a few bubbles show along the edges.
  3. FlipFlip and cook until golden on the underside. Browning too fast? Lower the heat — start medium, drop to medium-low. A smoking pan is a too-hot pan.
  4. RepeatWipe the pan clean and repeat with more oil and the remaining batter. Makes 9 pancakes — serves 3, three each.

From Monique Volz's Healthy Banana Oatmeal Pancakes (ambitiouskitchen.com/banana-oatmeal-pancakes) · The Hancox

Crazy Chocolate Cake

Daniel Amit's chocolate cake from foody — insanely moist, rich, and made for birthdays. The skewer comes out damp on purpose.

Tin31 × 22cm rectangular Hands-on≈ 20 min Bake40–45 min · see oven note Serves12

Ingredients

Cake
Ganache
UK shopping (house note — this is an Israeli recipe): Shokolit = sweetened chocolate drink powder — use drinking chocolate (e.g. Cadbury), NOT pure cocoa. This recipe names 38% sweet cream — UK whipping cream (~35%) is the nearest; double cream also works in the ganache.
Oven (house note): the original bakes at 160C fan. Use it as written on our fan setting, or 180C no fan. Ours runs cool either way, so trust the skewer: it should come out moist, not clean.

Method

  1. WhiskWhisk the eggs and sugar, by hand or in a mixer.
  2. Build the batterGradually add the rest — the oil, chocolate drink powder, flour, instant coffee and salt.
  3. Melt & foldIn a separate pan, melt the cream with the dark and milk chocolate. Once melted, add to the batter and mix until no lumps remain.
  4. BakePour into a greased 31 × 22cm tin and bake in the preheated oven 40–45 minutes (see the oven note). Take it out when a skewer comes out moist.
  5. GanacheMelt the cream with the milk and dark chocolate in a pan over low heat.
  6. Pour & sprinkleWhile the cake is still warm, cut it in the tin, pour the ganache all over, let it cool a little, and finish with colourful sprinkles.

Translated for The Hancox from Daniel Amit's chocolate cake (danielamit.foody.co.il) · 1M views, rated 4/5 by 933 home cooks · photo: our own bake

Double Chocolate & Mascarpone Traybake

Benjamina Ebuehi's one-bowl crowd cake from Guardian Feast — velvety crumb, milk-chocolate mascarpone frosting. Family-tested: "Very nice cake!"

Tin23 × 33cm, lined with overhang Prep20 min Cook40 min Serves16

Ingredients

Cake
Frosting
Oven (house note): the recipe's 180C conventional is our no-fan setting (or 160C fan) — ours runs cool, so expect the top of the 35–40 min window and trust the skewer.

Method

  1. Tin & ovenHeat the oven to 180C (160C fan) / gas 4. Grease a 23 × 33cm baking tin, then line with greaseproof paper, leaving enough overhang to lift the cake out once baked.
  2. MeltPut the chocolate and butter in a heatproof bowl and melt in short microwave bursts, or over a pan of simmering water. Set aside to cool.
  3. One-bowl batterIn a large bowl, mix the flour, cocoa, sugar, baking powder, bicarb and salt. Make a well in the centre, pour in the eggs, oil, milk and cooled chocolate-butter mix, and whisk to a thick, smooth batter. Pour in 150ml hot water and mix again until well combined.
  4. BakePour into the prepared tin and bake 35–40 minutes, until a skewer inserted into the middle comes out clean. Take out and leave to cool.
  5. Frosting basePut the chocolate, butter, cocoa, half the cream and the salt in a small saucepan and heat very gently until just melted.
  6. Whisk in mascarponePut the mascarpone in a bowl, pour the chocolate mixture over, and whisk well to combine. Add the rest of the cream, mix until smooth, then leave to cool and thicken to a spreadable consistency.
  7. Frost & finishSpread the frosting all over the top and sides, top with shaved chocolate, then cut into slices and serve.

From Benjamina Ebuehi's double chocolate and mascarpone traybake — Guardian Feast, The Sweet Spot (theguardian.com, 3 May 2024) · clipped from the paper & family-approved

Homemade Hummus

Efrat Siachi's ten-minute hummus from 10 Dakot — one UK tin of chickpeas, raw tahini, lemon and a clove of garlic, blitzed smooth in the food processor. Contains sesame.

Makes1 big bowl (≈ 500g) Hands-on10 min Ovennone — food processor Keeps5 days, fridge

Ingredients

Hummus
To serve
Scaled to a UK tin (house note — this is an Israeli recipe): the original is written for the Israeli 550g tin (290g drained) with 1 cup (240ml) tahini, 5 tbsp lemon, ½ tsp salt and ⅔ cup (160ml) water. A UK 400g tin drains to 240g, so everything here is scaled by 0.83. Tahini: the raw, runny Israeli-style kind (Al Arz / Har Bracha from the kosher shop or Amazon; Belazu or Lebanese brands from the supermarket) — not toasted or paste-stiff. The author's own swap: instead of the tin, 1¾ cups very soft cooked chickpeas; from frozen, boil until completely soft before blending.
Texture (author's tip): too thick → add water a tablespoon at a time; too loose → a few more chickpeas or a little more tahini. Use good raw tahini — it is most of the flavour.
Weaker food processor? Blitz the chickpeas and garlic first, then add the rest — makes sure the garlic and chickpeas are properly ground. A strong processor can take everything at once.

Method

  1. Drain & rinseTip the chickpeas into a sieve, drain, and rinse under the tap.
  2. BlitzPut the chickpeas and all the remaining ingredients in the food processor and blend to a smooth, creamy texture.
  3. Plate & serveSpread onto a plate, drizzle with olive oil and dust with ground cumin or sweet paprika; scatter a few whole chickpeas over if you have them. Best eaten straight away — it thickens and firms up a little once chilled. Serve with fresh pittas, a finely chopped salad and a hot salsa.
  4. KeepsIn a sealed box in the fridge for about 5 days.
Variations (from the author): spicy — a fresh chilli in the blend, or zhug on top · masabacha — stir some whole cooked chickpeas through part of the hummus · mushroom — sliced mushrooms fried with onion and garlic in olive oil, spooned over · with ful — cooked broad beans alongside, the traditional way.

Translated for The Hancox from Efrat Siachi's homemade hummus on 10 Dakot (10dakot.co.il, first published April 2016) · scaled ×0.83 to a UK 400g tin · Israeli cup = 240ml

Sticky Oven Chicken

Revital Federbush's "tastiest and quickest I've ever made" oven chicken — leg pieces in a four-ingredient tomato, soy, silan and garlic sauce, covered and roasted low, browned at the end. No searing, no marinating. Contains soya.

Serves5 · 10 pieces Hands-on≈ 10 min Oven2 h covered + 10 min browning Dishlidded oven pot or deep roasting tin

Ingredients

Chicken
Sauce
Optional
UK shopping (house note — this is an Israeli recipe): we use Ocado bone-in thighs and drumsticks — any mix to make 10 pieces. Drumsticks are smaller than a split leg quarter, so start checking the probe before the second hour is up. Silan = date syrup (Belazu or the kosher-shop bottle; honey works). Tomato purée from the tube is fine — the Israeli small tin is 100g. Soy sauce is the only salt, and standard soy sauce contains wheat.
Oven (house note): the recipe's temperatures are conventional — use our no-fan setting, or drop each one 20C on fan (200C / 130C / 160C). Ours runs cool, so trust the probe: the author cites the Israeli health ministry's 72C in the thickest part; UK FSA guidance is 75C (or 70C held for two minutes).
Don't wash the chicken (author, citing health authorities): rinsing doesn't clean it, it only spreads bacteria round the kitchen.

Method

  1. OvenHeat the oven to 220C conventional (not fan).
  2. Sauce in the tinMix all the sauce ingredients straight in the pot or tin you'll cook the chicken in — one less bowl.
  3. CoatLay the chicken pieces in and turn them thoroughly through the sauce (disposable gloves make this easy). Add the potatoes or sweet potatoes now if using.
  4. CoverLidded oven pot: put the lid on. No lid: lay a sheet of wet, crumpled baking paper over the chicken, then seal tightly with foil.
  5. Roast, covered1 hour at 220C, covered.
  6. Baste & drop the heatCheck the chicken and baste it with the sauce (for more sauce, add ½ cup water). Lower the oven to 150C and cook another hour, still covered. With potatoes in, it may need an extra hour, until they're soft.
  7. BrownRaise the oven to 180C, take the cover off and brown for about 10 minutes, until the chicken looks well coloured.
Why no searing (author, citing Harold McGee): browning chicken first to "seal in the juices" is a myth. The Maillard browning happens anyway above 140C, so a long roast gets you the same flavour — browning at the end is easier, less mess, and just as good. It adds flavour, not juiciness.

Translated for The Hancox from Revital Federbush's oven chicken on Matbach Kal (160cal.com, published April 2022, updated 2024) · author's figures: 229 kcal per portion, 13g fat, 13g carbs, 15g protein · Israeli cup = 240ml

Chicken, Leek & Cider Gratin

Rick Stein's Cornish gratin — browned chicken thigh and soft leeks in a cider, Dijon and cream sauce, topped with thinly sliced potatoes and cheddar and baked until bubbling. Contains milk, mustard and soya.

Serves4 Hands-on≈ 30 min Oven30 min Dishcasserole + 26 × 20cm ovenproof dish

Ingredients

Filling
Topping
Magimix (house note): the potatoes need to be very thin to cook through in 30 minutes — use the thinnest slicing disc. The same disc does the leeks, and the grating disc does the cheddar.
Allergens: milk (butter, cream, cheddar), mustard (Dijon), soya — and standard soy sauce also contains wheat. BBC Food lists it as egg-free and nut-free.
Cider: it boils for a few minutes and then bakes, but not all the alcohol cooks off — an alcohol-free cider is a straight swap if that matters.
Oven (house note): the recipe's 200C conventional is our no-fan setting (or 180C fan). Ours runs cool, so go by the potatoes: done when a knife slides through them easily.

Method

  1. OvenHeat the oven to 200C, no fan (180C fan / gas 6).
  2. Brown the chickenIn a large casserole over a medium heat, melt half the butter and fry the chicken until golden brown. Lift out onto a plate.
  3. Soften the leeksAdd the leeks and the rest of the butter to the pan and cook over a low heat until soft, without colouring.
  4. SauceAdd the cider, mustard, soy sauce, smoked paprika, cream, ½ tsp salt and a grind of pepper. Boil 2–3 minutes, until thickened and combined.
  5. Chicken back inReturn the chicken with its juices and stir to heat through. Tip into the ovenproof dish (about 26 × 20cm, or a 23cm round).
  6. TopLay the potato slices over the filling, overlapping. Scatter the cheddar and a pinch of smoked paprika.
  7. Bake30 minutes, until bubbling and the potatoes are tender when poked with a knife. Serve hot, with green leafy veg alongside.

Giraffe Malezit

The "Malaysian" from Giraffe, made at home: a blitzed pesto of basil, coriander, red curry paste and fried peanuts, onion softened in coconut cream, crunchy pepper and cucumber, sliced roast chicken and egg noodles, as Giraffe makes it. Coconut cream in place of the restaurant's cream. Contains peanuts, wheat and egg; check the curry paste for shrimp or fish.

Chicken≈ 20 min · 180C oven Woka few minutes, high heat Noodlesfresh egg, 2 × 275g KitMagimix or blender + wok

Ingredients

Pesto
Stir-fry
To garnish
Allergens: peanuts — in the pesto itself, not just on top, so they can't be left off; wheat and egg (egg noodles). Red curry paste: check the label — many Thai curry pastes contain shrimp or fish. Noodles: check the pack too — some noodles also contain soya or sesame.
Fried peanuts, not roasted (author): they taste different. She buys them in a bag from the neighbourhood grocery, and says nut stalls sell them too.
Finding fried peanuts in the UK (house note, unchecked): look for a pack whose ingredients say the peanuts are fried or cooked in oil.
Coconut cream, not cream (author): the restaurant dish uses cream; she finds that heavy, loves the sweetness of coconut cream, and always asked Giraffe to make it that way. You're welcome to swap back to cream if you prefer. We make it with coconut cream — and at Giraffe, ask for it with coconut cream instead of cream (house note).
Cooking with coconut cream (house note): it doesn't reduce and thicken the way dairy cream does — it loosens with heat and can turn oily or split if it boils hard for long. So keep the boil short, toss rather than simmer, and if it splits, take it off the heat and toss in a splash of water. It sets firm in the fridge, which is why leftovers need a little liquid.
UK shopping (house note — this is an Israeli recipe): the recipe's tin is the Israeli Mizrach uMaarav coconut cream, 400ml and 17–19% fat — the same size as a UK tin, so one tin covers both halves. Buy coconut cream, not coconut milk. Noodles: Giraffe's menu describes the dish as egg noodles (Giraffe online-menu screenshot, 2026-11-11), and its photo shows thin round ones — so we use fresh fine egg noodles. Dried medium egg noodles (e.g. Blue Dragon 250g) are the cupboard back-up — one 250g pack is our guess for this amount (dried noodles weigh much less than fresh), cooked as the pack says. Amount: the recipe's 3 Israeli ready-to-wok packs are ≈ 200g each (pack info supplied by Gilly), 600g in all — 2 × 275g (550g) is the nearest whole-pack match. Ginger is not specified — grated fresh is our reading.

Method

  1. ChickenSeason the breast with olive oil, salt and pepper and roast at 180C for about 20 minutes, until fully cooked — no pink in the middle and the juices run clear (with a probe, UK FSA: 75C in the thickest part). Slice into strips.
  2. NoodlesThe recipe's ready-to-wok noodles: soak in boiling water for 2 minutes, rinse and drain, then gently separate them with your hands. For fresh egg noodles, prepare them as the pack says (house note — we haven't checked the M&S pack).
  3. PestoBlitz all the pesto ingredients in the Magimix or a blender. Do it last, right before the wok — the basil darkens if the pesto sits (Oz Telem's tip from his version of this dish).
  4. OnionHeat neutral oil in the wok and add the onion. Pour in half the coconut cream (the second half of the tin) and cook over a medium heat for 1 minute. No need to sear it — just cooking it a little in the coconut cream gives it the sweetness that is typical of the dish.
  5. Pesto inAdd the pesto and turn the heat up. Stir for a few seconds. (House note: just until it bubbles — see the coconut-cream note.)
  6. Veg & chickenAdd the pepper, cucumber, beansprouts and chicken and toss. Don't let the veg soften — the point is that they stay crunchy and fresh.
  7. Noodles & serveAdd the noodles, mix well and serve piping hot with a handful of coriander and crushed peanuts.
Drying out? (author): keep the wok hot, but if the liquid evaporates and it turns dry, drop the heat for a moment, add a little coconut cream or even a splash of water, turn it back up and stir.
Leftovers (author): add a little liquid and stir-fry again — not in the microwave.
Chicken leftovers (house note, UK food-safety guidance): into the fridge within 2 hours, reheat only once, and until steaming hot all the way through.

Translated for The Hancox from Dana Moyal Reicher's recreation of Giraffe's "Malaysian" (Instagram @danareicher, reel C6f0MbAoxY8 — worked out from hours at the pass questioning the cooks), with the pesto-timing tip from Oz Telem's version on The Kitchen Coach · photo: Giraffe's menu shot of the restaurant dish — swap for ours when made · Israeli cup = 240ml
